reasoning_notes.reasoning: With no history, bidding 20 maximizes profit if the others bid higher, while preserving the option to adapt after observing their bids. Lower bids sacrifice margin without evidence they are needed.
With no history, the other firms’ bids are unknown. The top bid preserves a positive margin if I win, while avoiding an unsupported low-price commitment; ties still earn profit.
With no history and no disclosed final round, start at the highest bid to earn the largest margin if competitors also bid high; public outcomes will inform later bids.
